texts.preamble: Abraham K U --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 5 August, 2023 In The Court Of Harvinder Singh, Presiding Officer : Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01, (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi. Award/Judgment
texts.facts: CASE OF PETITIONER SIDE 2. Succinctly, the case put forward by petition/DAR is that on 23.10.2015 injured Abraham K U along with other persons were going on a tour to Manali in a hired Tempo Traveler bearing registration No. DL-1VA-8948 which was being driven by Kamal Garg. At about 1:10 AM, their vehicle reached at Tax Barier, Near Prem Dhaba, P.S. Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab. A truck bearing registration No. HP69A7149 was parked in the middle of Abraham K U --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 5 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105685892/ 3 the road in rash and negligent manner without any indication or parking lights or reflector in the complete darkness at that place. Due to same, their vehicle bearing registration No. DL1VA8948 struck against said vehicle No. HP69A7149. As a consequence, all the occupants of tempo traveler sustained various injuries. Driver/Kamal Garg and Mrs Maya Abraham died due to same. The incident happened solely due to rash and negligent driving/parking of respondent no.01 who has wrongly parked his vehicle in the middle of the road without any indicators/reflectors. Injured was doing catering work and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month at the time of incident. The respondent no.01 being driver, the respondent no.02 being owner and respondent no.03 being the insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner(s). The applicant(s)/claimant(s) has/have sought compensation of Rs.51,50,000/- (Rupees Fifty One Lakhs and Fifty Thousand Only) from the respondents. MISCELLANEOUS PROCEEDINGS 3. Notice of the application/petition/DAR was issued to the respondents on which they appeared and filed their WS(s)/reply(ies) to the present petition/application. RESPONSE OF RESPONDENT NO.01 &02 4. In gist, the response of the respondent no.01 & 02 as discernible from their reply/written statement is that the respondent no.1 was having a valid driving licence to drive truck bearing registration No. HP69A7149 at the time of incident. Vehicle in question was duly insured with the respondent No.3 covering the date of accident. There was no negligence on the part of the respondent no.1. One set of rear tyres of their vehicle has brusted and its excel has also broken down. Respondent no.1 has parked their vehicle to the left side of the road. Respondent no.1 took all safety measures by giving regular hazardous light. He also put some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters can make out that their vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Deceased driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948 was driving at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle from behind. Incident took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948. With these averments, respondent no. 1 & 2 have prayed for dismissal of the same. RESPONSE OF RESPONDENT NO.03 5. In gist, the response of the respondent no.03 as discernible from its reply/written statement is that Incident in question took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased driver of vehicle bearing registration No. DL1VA-8948(Tempo Traveler). Vehicle bearing registration No. HP69A7149 (HGV- Abraham K U --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 5 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105685892/ 4 Abraham K U Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. [MACT No.477647/2016] Page No.5 of 29 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.07 16:38:17 +0530 Truck) was insured with it vide policy no. 42103/31/15/630002778 for period 03.08.2015 to 02.08.2016 in the name of Sh. Shankar Ram. With these main contentions, respondent No.3 prayed for dismissal of the present petition. ISSUES 6.1 OPP. 2. OPP 3. Relief. 6.2 Thereafter, matter was fixed for evidence of petitioner side. PETITIONER SIDE EVIDENCE 7.1 The petitioner(s)/claimant(s) examined himself as PW1 to establish his claim. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A reiterating and supporting the contents of their application/petition. He relied upon the documents i.e. attested copy of charge sheet along with all the documents Ex.PW1/1, family photocographs Ex.PW1/2, copy of Election I Card of his deceased wife Ex.PW1/3, pay slip of his deceased wife of the month of September 2015 Ex.PW1/4, copies of Abraham K U Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. PW1 was cross- examined at length by Ld. Counsels for the respondent side which is not reproduced herein for sake of brevity and was discharged. 7.2 No other witness was examined by petitioner side qua present matter, petitioner side evidence was closed vide order dated 07.03.2022 and thereafter, matter was fixed for respondent side evidence. The respondent no.01 examined himself as R1W1 in connected MACT Petition No. 476356/2016 in case "Santosh vs. Ravi Sharma & ors", and same was ordered to be read in present matter also vide orders dated 02.06.2022. He in gist vide affidavit of evidence Ex.R1W1/A deposed that there was no negligence on his part. 8.2 The respondent no.02 examined himself as R2W1 in connected MACT Petition No. 476356/2016 in case "Santosh vs. Ravi Sharma & ors" and same was ordered to be read in present matter also vide orders dated 02.06.2022. He in gist vide affidavit of evidence Ex.R2W1/A deposed that there was no negligence on part of respondent no.1. Respondent no.1 parked the vehicle on the left side of road and adopted all safely measures like, giving regular hazardous light, putting some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters should come to know that the vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL- 1VA-8948 was driving it at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle in question from behind. R1W1 was examined and discharged. 8.3 Respondent no.03 examined ASI Khushal Singh of PS City Ropar, District Ropar, Punjab as R3W1 who in gist, has deposed that he was not the IO of the case arising out of FIR No. 112 in question dated 23.10.2015. He was only assisting the IO in the said case. They received information about the accident from the Civil Hospital, Ropar District Roop Nagar, Punjab at around 12:00 noon on 23.10.2015. He accompanied IO ASI Sarabjeet to the Civil Hospital, Ropar where they recorded the statement of Ms. Reena Raju pertaining to the accident. They reached at the spot of accident at about 4:00 PM after getting conducted the post mortem of two deceased/victims of the incident. 9.2 Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.01 and 02 are that deceased driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL- 1VA-8948 was himself driving his vehicle at a very high speed, in a rash manner and negligent manner. The petition of the petitioner side may be dismissed.
texts.arguments: 11.2 Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its division bench decision in matter of "Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors." (2011) 1 SCC 343 has held : - "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : Abraham K U Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of "Sarla Verma Vs. DTC" 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim.
